Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Ask: Finovate Bank requires either 0-retention of request/response content or a very short retention window for any PII-containing traffic. You also need EU data residency and audit logs for 90 days for compliance.
- What we discussed: Redwood can support per-route retention policies and model-level redaction. For hosted customers, default logging retains minimal telemetry for 30 days; for Dedicated/Private we can offer more control.
- Open items: exact retention window you need for non-billing logs, whether 0-retention must apply to all incoming request content, and whether Finovate can do client-side redaction before sending.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can loop in Dev (technical) + Laura (sales ops) to outline the feasible retention options and tradeoffs.
2) If you need 0-retention on hosted, we should confirm whether that requirement is absolute or if a 7-day encrypted, access-restricted window is acceptable for audit purposes.
3) I'll attach our data retention options + SOC2 report for legal review (see attachments).

Would you be able to confirm which of these is mandatory vs nice-to-have by EOD tomorrow? Happy to set up a short call with Dev to go over technical controls.

Best,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from Legal and Product: 

- 0-retention is our preference for any raw customer input that contains PII. For enrichment/ML purposes we cannot retain any raw inputs longer than 24 hours unless it's been tokenized and irreversibly pseudonymized.
- Audit logs (who called what API / success/failure) must be available to us for 90 days. Those logs should not contain request/response bodies.
- Data residency: all data for EU customers must remain in our EU tenant/region.

Legal will review SOC2 but they will also want a written exception path if we request any deviation from 0-retention. Can you outline what options are available for hosted accounts vs Dedicated/Private deployments?

Thanks — Elena
Elena Kovacs

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Looping in Dev and Laura to confirm technical feasibility and options.

Elena — high level:
- Hosted API: we offer configurable retention policies down to 7 days for request/response content, with PII redaction tooling and encrypted at-rest storage. We do not currently offer true 0-retention (no storage of user content) in hosted mode because we rely on short-term KV caches and telemetry for service reliability.
- Dedicated: with a Dedicated plan we can implement stricter controls, including auto-purge pipelines and customer-managed keys; in some cases we can support customer-requested retention windows shorter than 7 days, subject to architecture review.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control — Finovate can require 0-retention by configuring the runtime to not persist request/response content and to disable telemetry exports that include content.

Dev — can you outline the technical tradeoffs (availability, debuggability, and fallback behavior) if we enforce 0-retention for a subset of routes? Also, what would it take to support a 24-hour maximum retention for pseudonymized inputs in hosted?

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi all — quick technical notes and options (TL;DR at the top):

TL;DR:
- Hosted: minimum practical retention for request/response content is 7 days with strict access controls and encryption; we can support PII redaction and field-level tokenization before persistence. Audit logs (no bodies) can be kept 90+ days.
- Dedicated: we can implement a 24-hour retention with a custom purge job and customer-managed KMS, subject to an architecture review and a small professional services engagement.
- Private: full 0-retention possible (requires configuration changes and disabling some centralized telemetry; we provide a checklist).

Details:
1) Why hosted can't be immediate 0-retention: our serving runtime uses short-lived KV caches and request tracing to enable high-quality session resumption and to debug failures. Removing all storage of content would increase failure investigation time and could impact model quality for multi-turn sessions.
2) Pseudonymization: we can offer server-side pseudonymization where PII fields are replaced with irreversible tokens before persistence. For financial PII we recommend client-side redaction as the most robust approach.
3) Audit logs: we can guarantee 90-day retention for operational metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model used, latency, error codes) without bodies.
4) Implementation path for Finovate:
   - Option A (Hosted - near-term): 7-day retention with server-side pseudonymization + field-level redaction; SOC2 evidence provided.
   - Option B (Dedicated - preferred): 24-hour retention with customer-managed keys and automated purge; requires kickoff and architecture review.
   - Option C (Private): 0-retention enforced by configuration; we provide a deployment checklist and a support window for cutover.

Next steps I recommend: a short technical workshop (30 min) between Dev and Finovate engineers to validate Option B feasibility. If Legal needs written exception language, I can produce a technical appendix describing purge guarantees and controls.

Attachment: soc2-report-2025.pdf (redacted summary for customers)

Thanks, Dev and Marissa — that is helpful. A few items from Legal/Product after reviewing: 

- Finovate prefers Option B (Dedicated) if the timeline and cost make sense. We need a written guarantee of a 24-hour retention window for request/response content and a documented purge process.
- If Dedicated is not immediately available, we can accept Option A as an interim with the caveat that any stored content must be pseudonymized and that we will require a SOC2+ addendum stating retention limits.
- Please send a proposed statement of work (SOW) / architecture review scope and an estimate for the Dedicated path. Also include the technical appendix for purge guarantees for Legal to review.

Can we target a technical workshop next week (April 6 or 7)?

Regards,
Elena
